prose: The company behind July's first public disclosure of an autonomous agent cyberattack shares three lessons. First: much more transparency is needed in AI. The author wonders what would have happened had they not disclosed - especially now that similar incidents are known to have been happening months earlier, in secret, at a handful of frontier labs without monitoring.

To understand and mitigate these emerging cybersecurity risks, the piece argues, the global community needs stronger standards for monitoring and incident disclosure - for example, mandatory sharing of full agent traces.
highlights: Lessons from the first disclosed autonomous agent cyberattack (July).
Lesson one: AI needs much more transparency.
Similar incidents happened months earlier in secret at frontier labs.
Calls for stronger monitoring and incident-disclosure standards.
Suggests mandatory sharing of full agent traces.
